recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中央有兩顆大型細胞，淡灰紫色胞質豐富且邊界圓滑，核卵圓、染色質細緻，比周圍的淋巴球與顆粒球前驅細胞大數倍，呈現增生組織球（reactive histiocytes）的樣子。
features: Large histiocytes with abundant, pale gray-lilac, finely granular to slightly vacuolated cytoplasm and smooth round outlines
Oval, eccentric nuclei with finely reticular chromatin and no prominent nucleoli
Low N:C ratio with ill-defined outer cytoplasmic margins
Background of small lymphocytes, plasmacytoid cells, granulocytic precursors and erythroid cells
No ingested blood cells or organisms evident
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows scattered large histiocytes with abundant pale gray-lilac, finely granular cytoplasm and oval eccentric nuclei with fine chromatin and inconspicuous nucleoli. No phagocytosed cells, pigment or organisms are identified within these cells. The background contains small lymphocytes, granulocytic precursors and erythroid elements without increased blasts. Findings are consistent with reactive histiocytes; clinical correlation for infection, inflammation or hemophagocytic syndrome is recommended.

ddx.vs: Hemophagocytes contain engulfed erythrocytes, platelets or nucleated cells, which are not seen in these histiocytes.
Plasma cells are smaller with deeply basophilic cytoplasm, a perinuclear hof and clock-face chromatin rather than abundant pale cytoplasm.
Osteoblasts have eccentric nuclei with a pale Golgi zone set away from the nucleus and more basophilic cytoplasm, often in clusters.
Mast cells have cytoplasm packed with dark purple metachromatic granules obscuring the nucleus.
